title: No chain module in the player
text: The released player is the network alone. On the chain exam rl-v1's champion picks the coin-best action 91.6% of the time, but with a turn planner (value judge or coins judge, K=32) or a chain rule choosing its actions it scored 48.8%, 48.5%, 48.2% (engine kingdoms) and 49.9% head to head against itself without it.
rejected: A statistical turn planner at play time (no gain, 20x slower); a hand-written chain rule (changed 15 of 6,335 decisions).

title: Start from rl-v1's checkpoint, widened with the helper inputs
text: rl-v1 r2 was still improving when it stopped (67% to 81% vs GA over 2,200 iterations), and the helper inputs lifted rl-v2 by 3 points. Weights and Adam state loaded; new inputs at zero weight.
rejected: From zero (rl-v2 plateaued at ~74%); imitation of the GA (rl-v1 already did that).

title: Curriculum ends against the champion
text: Stage 1 rl-v1's own league (gate 84% vs GA), stage 2 + the frozen champion as 25% of games (gate 56% vs it), stage 3 open league with rl-v2 too. rl-v1 learned to beat az-v1 only once az-v1 was in its league.

title: Card school for cards the champion never tried
text: The card audit: Chapel never bought, Mine/Library/Moneylender bought in 4% of games, Council Room/Smithy/Village/Merchant 10-16%. In 15% of training games (stages 2-3) the learner's first buys are forced to 2 copies of one of 10 such cards, not recorded, so it learns to play them while buying stays its own choice.
rejected: Recording the forced buys (wrong PPO ratios); a starting deck with the card (changes the rules).

title: Card drill (run c2) for the cards the model loses against
text: 64,000 games of c1's net 2363 against 8 opponents (results/card_losses/): no card it cannot manage (worst: 3-4 points lower win rate with the card in the kingdom). Paired against rl-v1's champion on the same games, it gained most on the card-school cards (Chapel +10, Village +5, Festival +4 points) and is weaker on Sentry and Gardens (-5), Militia (-3), Witch, Harbinger, Workshop, Vassal, Mine, Bureaucrat. Run c2 continues from c1's iteration 2363 (net and Adam): the same open league and card school, plus a drill in 30% of the games on a kingdom with one of 10 such cards (30% the learner forced to 2 copies, 30% a net opponent forced, 40% free); learning rate 3e-4 to 2e-4 so it keeps what it knows.
rejected: Only more kingdoms with the cards (each is already in 38% of kingdoms); a new run from rl-v1 (would lose c1's gains).
